scope: All 176 numbered question groups in every English-language exam-paper variant listed for 2020–2025. Multi-part questions are summarised as a group; original PDFs and matching schemes remain authoritative. Irish-language PDFs are archived but are not separately translated or cross-mapped.
method: Educator review of extracted English papers and marking schemes; original skill summaries, with start pages checked against PDF page markers. Selected diagram pages visually inspected. No prediction of future paper content.

marking_guidance.principle: Use the scheme for the same year, level and question. Its examples are not exhaustive, and official examiners apply trained judgement. Course scores are formative; past rubrics do not predict future allocations.
marking_guidance.evidence: All English marking schemes, PDF page 2.

marking_guidance.principle: Write each requested output in execution order with the same line breaks as the program. Correct values alone can lose credit if layout changes meaning.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2025 Higher Q1, scheme PDF page 4; 2024 Ordinary Q1, scheme PDF page 4.

marking_guidance.principle: Show intermediate trace rows and sorting passes, not only the final answer. Schemes often recognise individual correct rows or steps.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2021 Higher Q5 and Q14; 2025 Higher Q14(a)(ii); 2025 Ordinary Q11.

marking_guidance.principle: When asked to name and explain, give a specific component, principle, role or risk and then connect it to the supplied scenario. Naming alone may satisfy only part of the rubric.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2025 Higher Q12 and Q13; 2024 Ordinary Q14.

marking_guidance.principle: Balanced discussion needs relevant benefits and drawbacks, with reasons and affected stakeholders. It is more than a list of fashionable technologies.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2020 Higher Q14(c); 2021 Higher Q15(c); 2023 Higher Q13(c); 2024 Higher Q13(c).

marking_guidance.principle: Section C uses graded response scales in which partial progress can receive credit; save an executable attempt and complete independently achievable requirements. Scale labels and thresholds vary by year.
marking_guidance.evidence: English marking schemes, Section C scale tables on PDF page 3 and question-specific descriptors.

marking_guidance.principle: Keep whole-string score adjustments outside a character loop when they should apply only once.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2020 Higher Q16(a)(vi): scheme explicitly withholds full credit for placing the solution inside the character loop.

marking_guidance.principle: Analyse the algorithm actually supplied. The fixed-pass bubble sort in 2024 is quadratic in both best and worst cases; early termination is an improvement, not an assumption about that code.
For median code, sort first and handle empty, odd-length and even-length lists separately; the 2025 task prohibits a library median function.
marking_guidance.evidence: 2025 Higher Q16(b), paper PDF pages 8–9 and corresponding scheme.

source_notes: The 2020 listing contains Higher Level material only. No Ordinary Level files or Irish Higher marking scheme are listed for that year.
Irish Ordinary Level marking schemes are absent from the 2024 and 2025 listings. No missing variant has been fabricated.
English and Irish paper files are retained exactly as downloaded; language variants have not been exhaustively compared.
Year-specific instructions differ: Section C carries 50 marks in 2021–2022 and 80 marks in 2020 and 2023–2025. Follow the printed instructions for each practice paper.

2024 Ordinary marking scheme Q10 describes a missing transport entry using a different person name than the visible source table. Use the source table and teacher judgement rather than memorising the label.
Some PDF text extraction loses diagram labels or scrambles headings; the original PDFs remain the reference for diagrams and exact wording.
